solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dancing is out after swelling puffed up (9)

indicatorNotes.Dancing: Letters that are dancing move about and land in a new order.
indicatorNotes.after: What comes after is placed second, so the jumbled IS OUT follows the swelling.

blocks.note: a bump is a swelling, as on the head

annotation.surface: Someone at a dance who is sitting it out because of a swollen ankle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dancing is out' reads as one phrase, but 'Dancing' works on 'is out' alone, and 'after' puts that jumble behind BUMP.
annotation.definitionFit: A bumptious person is self-important, puffed up with their own worth.

entries.clue: Two lads, the first one stunted — hardly any matter! (5)

indicatorNotes.stunted: Something stunted is kept short, so the word loses its end.

blocks.note: the first of the two lads, BOY, cut short

annotation.surface: Two young brothers, one of them small for his age, dismissed as not mattering.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two lads' supplies two words, BOY and SON, and only the first is docked. Bosons carry force rather than making up matter, which is the scientific joke in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A boson is a force-carrying particle, not really a building block of matter at all.

entries.clue: Plant deliveries not allowing a run on hospital ventilation (10)

blocks.note: in cricket a maiden is an over of six balls from which the batsmen score no runs
to air a room is to ventilate it

annotation.surface: A hospital that turned away deliveries that would have run the ventilation plant.
annotation.walkthrough: The deliveries are bowled balls, not parcels: a maiden over is a set of cricket deliveries off which no run is scored.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this fern, named for its fine hair-like stalks, is one kind of plant.

entries.clue: Time proverbially not on our side? (3,5)

annotation.definition: Time proverbially not on our side?
annotation.surface: A reflection that time is not on our side.
annotation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'time is the enemy'; 'not on our side' describes an enemy and also plays on the saying 'time is on our side'.
annotation.definitionFit: A description, not a synonym: whoever is not on our side is the opposing side, and the proverb gives time that role.

blocks.note: points to a well-worn saying about time, the kind that casts it as a character
echoes the hopeful 'time is on our side'; the setter means a foe, the side ranged against us

entries.clue: Start in place for shooting (5)

blocks.note: a plain synonym: the beginning of something, as of winter or an illness
split 3-and-2: where a film actor stands while the cameras roll

annotation.surface: A marksman taking up position to begin firing.
annotation.walkthrough: The shooting is filming, not firing: an actor who is on set is in place for the cameras.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a beginning, while the split reading is where an actor waits to be filmed.

entries.clue: Crass cake smashing competitions you’ll have in the bag? (4,5)

annotation.definition: competitions you’ll have in the bag?

indicatorNotes.smashing: What is smashed breaks into pieces that can be put back in another order.

annotation.surface: Contests in cake-smashing, a crude party game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the bag' usually means a win is assured; here the competitors are literally standing in sacks.
annotation.definitionFit: In a sack race each runner hops along with their legs inside a sack.

entries.clue: Be indebted to group behind European politician giving authority (10)

indicatorNotes.behind: What comes behind is placed after, so OWE and RING follow E and MP.

blocks.note: to owe is to be in debt
a ring is a group, as of dealers or spies

annotation.surface: A Euro-politician who owes favours to a faction and so hands it power.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue gives OWE RING first, then says it goes behind E MP, so the answer is built back to front from the clue's order.
annotation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to give them authority to act.

entries.clue: Board member formerly with European Commission (4)

annotation.surface: A director who used to sit on the European Commission.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the business sense of board, a company's directors, not a plank.
annotation.definitionFit: An exec, short for executive, often sits on a company board.

entries.clue: Delayed crossing delta from the south, missing hotel pool (6)

indicatorNotes.crossing: One word crossing another sits across it, so D goes inside.
indicatorNotes.from the south: In a down answer, read from the south means read from the bottom up.
indicatorNotes.missing: Missing a letter means it has gone.

blocks.note: H, hotel in the radio alphabet, is dropped

annotation.surface: A late-running traveller crossing the Nile delta from the south, having missed the hotel pool.
annotation.walkthrough: Both delta and hotel are radio-alphabet letters, D and H, rather than places on a trip. ELDDUP read upward gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the small sense: a little pool of rainwater on the ground.

entries.clue: Exhausted Republican breaks habit with barbarian spree (4,2,1,7)

indicatorNotes.breaks: R breaks into the word, splitting it.

blocks.note: to go on the razzle is British slang for going on a drinking spree

annotation.surface: A tired politician whose routine is shattered by a wild night out with a thug.
annotation.walkthrough: WONT is an old word for habit, and to be on the razzle is British slang for a drinking spree.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: frazzled means frayed to threads, and being worn to that state is being utterly exhausted.

entries.clue: Illicit profiting from wheel-turning mechanism, and pinions replaced by rear of axle (12)

indicatorNotes.replaced by: What is replaced is taken out and the new letter put in its place.

blocks.note: rack-and-pinion steering turns a car's front wheels
the run of letters AND PINIONS comes out, straddling the join into STEERING
the last letter of axle goes into the gap

annotation.surface: A mechanic's note on reworking a steering system, with the pinions swapped for a part at the back of the axle.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue's own 'and' is part of what is removed: AND PINIONS lifts out of RACK AND PINION STEERING, taking the S of STEERING with it.
annotation.definitionFit: Racketeering is making money from illegal schemes such as extortion.

entries.clue: A river repeatedly goes over here (7)

annotation.definition: A river repeatedly goes over here

indicatorNotes.goes over: To go over is to turn over, so the letters are read backwards.

annotation.surface: A description of a great waterfall, where a river keeps pouring over the edge.
annotation.walkthrough: A R AGAIN written backwards gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes Niagara Falls, where a river goes over the edge without stopping.
annotation.definitionFit: Niagara is both a river and the falls it goes over, endlessly.

entries.clue: Clearing assessment when learner leaves for start in college (10)

indicatorNotes.leaves for: L leaves and the other letter comes in for it, taking its place.
indicatorNotes.start in: The start of a word is its first letter.

blocks.note: the L on a learner driver's plates

annotation.surface: A college assessment in which a trainee is sent packing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Learner leaves for' is a swap, not a removal: one letter goes out and another comes into its slot.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: clearing a building means getting everyone out of it.

entries.clue: Trace 22nd letter about someone living in a dump (7)

indicatorNotes.about: One word placed about another goes round it.

blocks.note: V, the 22nd letter of the alphabet, spelt out
Stig of the Dump is a British children's book about a caveman living in a chalk pit used as a rubbish tip

annotation.surface: A trace of the letter V found on someone who lives in a rubbish tip.
annotation.walkthrough: The 22nd letter is written out as a word so it can go round the dump-dweller.
annotation.definitionFit: A vestige is a trace of something that has otherwise gone.

entries.clue: I follow vocal instruction to extract sap from coniferous wood? (9)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is what a successor says of themselves; the answer is the noun naming that person.

indicatorNotes.vocal: Vocal means spoken, so the answer is what the instruction sounds like.

blocks.clueFragment: instruction to extract sap from coniferous wood
blocks.note: cedar is a coniferous wood, and sucking is one way to extract sap

annotation.surface: A forester following orders to draw sap from pine trees.
annotation.walkthrough: The instruction is 'suck cedar', which spoken aloud runs together as SUCCEEDER.
annotation.definitionFit: A succeeder is one who succeeds, that is, comes after or follows someone.

entries.clue: Tea at high volume that’s worth little (5)

blocks.note: char or cha is British slang for tea
fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

annotation.surface: A cheap cup of tea served in a noisy room.
annotation.walkthrough: CHA is the British slang for tea, and FF is the musical mark fortissimo.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym by extension: the husks threshed from grain are worthless, so the word covers anything of little value.

entries.clue: Complimentary hairdresser’s offering to improvise (9)

annotation.surface: A free haircut offered by a stylist who makes it up as they go.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complimentary' means free of charge, not full of praise.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rappers and dancers who make it up on the spot are said to do exactly this.

entries.clue: Critical democrat not available to keep two conservatives apart (12)

indicatorNotes.to keep: What keeps something holds it within.
indicatorNotes.apart: Two things kept apart have something between them.

blocks.note: a Tory is a British Conservative

annotation.surface: A critical Democrat, too busy to be the go-between keeping two Conservatives apart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two conservatives' names two different words, and the democrat and 'not available' sit between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Condemnatory remarks are critical, expressing condemnation.

entries.clue: Hot emotional intensity in total (3,3,4)

blocks.note: read literally: all of the rage, the whole of the anger

annotation.surface: A burst of strong feeling that runs hot.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase at face value, rage being intense emotion and 'all the' being the total of it.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something fashionable is hot property, and the literal reading is the whole of one's anger.

entries.clue: Red-stained flower almost perished (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: Almost the word is the word without its last letter.

annotation.surface: A red-stained flower that has nearly died.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Almost' belongs to the flower, not to 'perished'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stained with blood, which is red.

entries.clue: Former president’s wretched ball and chain on arm (7,7)

indicatorNotes.wretched: Something in a wretched state is in a mess, the letters disordered.

annotation.surface: A former president shackled with a miserable ball and chain on his arm.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'and' in 'ball and chain' is not fodder: BALL plus CHAIN ON ARM makes exactly fourteen letters. A 'ball and chain' is also slang for a wife.
annotation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth president of the United States.

entries.clue: Terrier vs Terries in a tangle (9)

indicatorNotes.in a tangle: Letters in a tangle are twisted into a new order.

annotation.surface: A dog-fight between a terrier and a pack of Terries, all tangled up.
annotation.walkthrough: A Terrier here is not a dog but a member of Britain's Territorial Army, its part-time volunteer reserve.
annotation.definitionFit: A Terrier, a Territorial Army soldier, is a reservist.

entries.clue: Smearing Fife, a cynic not working (10)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a gerund phrase; the answer is the noun for that state.

indicatorNotes.Smearing: Letters that are smeared are smudged out of shape.

annotation.surface: A jobless cynic from Fife spreading slander.
annotation.walkthrough: Fife is a region of Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: Inefficacy is the failure of something to produce its intended effect, its not working.

entries.clue: Butler maybe getting page out of Spanish paper for French writer (8)

indicatorNotes.getting: Getting joins one part to the next.
indicatorNotes.out of: P is taken out of the paper's name.

blocks.note: Rab Butler was a leading British Conservative politician of the 1950s

annotation.surface: A butler fetching a Spanish newspaper, minus a page, for a French author.
annotation.walkthrough: Butler is a surname, not a servant, and 'maybe' warns that Rab is one example of a Butler.
annotation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the French Renaissance author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

entries.clue: Hugging old sailors, with bristles, in a stiff way (10)

indicatorNotes.Hugging: One word hugging another wraps round it.

blocks.note: stubbly means bristly, so with bristles

annotation.surface: Unshaven old sailors hugged awkwardly.
annotation.walkthrough: The hugging word, 'with bristles', comes after what it hugs in the clue, and old sailors is two abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: Stiff here means obstinate, and doing something stubbornly is doing it in an unbending way.

entries.clue: Not yet having left home, shortly drop in (6)

indicatorNotes.shortly: Shortly means in a shortened form, so a letter is cut off the end.

blocks.note: still, as in 'still here', cut short

annotation.surface: Someone still at home, told to pop round shortly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drop in' looks like a visit, but it is the literal sense of instil: to put in drop by drop.
annotation.definitionFit: Instil comes from the Latin for putting in by drops, as with eye drops.

entries.clue: Small arm aristocrat carries when leading riot (10)

indicatorNotes.carries: What carries something holds it inside.

blocks.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
as meaning at the time when
something very funny is a riot, or a hoot

annotation.surface: A nobleman armed with a small gun at the head of a riot.
annotation.walkthrough: A riot here is not unrest but great fun; both a riot and a hoot mean something hilarious.
annotation.definitionFit: A peashooter is a toy tube for blowing peas, a very small arm indeed.

entries.clue: One of the Reds welcomes good sport (5)

indicatorNotes.welcomes: What welcomes something takes it in.

blocks.note: a ruby is a red gem

annotation.surface: A Liverpool player welcoming a good sport.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Reds' suggests a football club such as Liverpool, but it only means red things.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the rugby codes, union and league, are among Britain's major team sports.

entries.clue: Auditor’s man had to cover inside advice (9)

indicatorNotes.Auditor’s: An auditor is a hearer, so the words are as heard.

blocks.note: guy is a man, and guy'd is guy had
to line something is to cover its inside

annotation.surface: An accountant's employee who was told to take on some internal checks.
annotation.walkthrough: The auditor is a listener, not an accountant: only 'man had' is heard.
annotation.definitionFit: A guideline is a piece of advice on how to act.

entries.clue: Facing punishment to achieve bar clearance? (3,3,4,4)

blocks.note: British idiom for being in serious trouble
high jumpers must clear a bar

annotation.surface: Someone in trouble who has to clear the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar clearance' could be a pub closing, but it is the athletics bar.
annotation.definitionFit: To be for the high jump is to be due for punishment; the idiom first meant due to be hanged.

entries.clue: We back away from Notts town informer (4)

indicatorNotes.back: Back means written backwards, so WE becomes EW.
indicatorNotes.away from: Letters away from a word are removed from it.

blocks.note: Newark is a market town in Nottinghamshire
WE reversed, the letters that go

annotation.surface: Townsfolk shunning a local informer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'We back' supplies letters in reverse order, and those are what leave the town's name.
annotation.definitionFit: A nark is British slang for a police informer.

entries.clue: Tossed fragments of tin etc after refining (8)

indicatorNotes.after refining: Refined material has been reworked, so the letters are reordered.

annotation.surface: Scraps thrown out of a metal refinery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like the link between definition and wordplay, but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Confetti is little pieces of paper tossed over a bride and groom.

entries.clue: Emma in films, however acting to entertain politicians (8)

indicatorNotes.to entertain: To entertain guests is to have them in, so MPS sits inside the pair THO ON.

blocks.note: an actor who is on is performing

annotation.surface: An actor performing for a group of politicians.
annotation.walkthrough: 'However acting' makes a pair that wraps round the politicians, with the join between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Emma Thompson is a British film actress.

entries.clue: Complex variable pair opposed to some number dividing half of cube (9)

indicatorNotes.dividing: What divides a word splits it by going inside.
indicatorNotes.half of: Half of a four-letter word is two letters, here the back half.

blocks.note: in algebra y and z are unknowns, a pair of variables
n stands for an unspecified number

annotation.surface: A mathematics problem about variables and a number dividing a cube.
annotation.walkthrough: Every maths word is really letters: algebra symbols for the variables and the number, and 'half of cube' is two letters split by the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Byzantine means intricately complex, after the elaborate bureaucracy of Byzantium.

entries.clue: Extract iodine collected by Geiger, possibly radioactive, leaving dig (8,4)

indicatorNotes.collected by: What is collected by something is gathered inside it.

blocks.note: Hans Geiger, of the Geiger counter

annotation.surface: Taking a sample of radioactive iodine with a Geiger counter.
annotation.walkthrough: Geiger is a first-name clue: 'possibly' marks HANS as one Geiger among many.
annotation.definitionFit: A Parthian shot is a cutting remark made on leaving, like the Parthian archers who fired while riding away.

entries.clue: The speaker’s to perform in a tick, short of dramatic high point (9)

indicatorNotes.in: One thing in another sits inside it.
indicatorNotes.short: Short means cut off at the end.

blocks.note: I'M, what the speaker says of themselves
a click, a ticking sound, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone about to give a performance at the climax of a play in a moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The speaker's' is not a homophone signal but I'M, the speaker's 'I am'. 'In a tick' looks like 'in a moment', but the tick is a click which holds IMACT.
annotation.definitionFit: Climactic means forming a climax, the dramatic high point.

entries.clue: Soviet official’s order to overlook breaking wheels (9)

indicatorNotes.breaking: What breaks a word goes inside it, splitting it.

blocks.note: wheels is slang for a car
the Order of Merit, a British honour
to miss something is to overlook it

annotation.surface: A Soviet official ordering someone to ignore a broken-down vehicle.
annotation.walkthrough: Wheels is slang for a car, and the order is the British Order of Merit.
annotation.definitionFit: A commissar was a Communist Party official in the Soviet Union.

entries.clue: There’s whiskey in odd roll transported from Eurasia (3-5)

indicatorNotes.in: W is put in the jumbled letters.
indicatorNotes.transported: Letters that are transported are carried to new positions.

annotation.surface: A strange bread roll with whisky in it, imported from Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd' is not the anagram signal here; it is fodder, and 'transported' does the rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: The Old World is Europe, Asia and Africa, as against the Americas.

entries.clue: What may improve view of people like Deighton? (4)

blocks.note: glass that sharpens or magnifies sight
Len Deighton, the British spy novelist; people sharing his first name, made plural

annotation.surface: A question about what might raise one's opinion of Len Deighton's fans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'View of people' reads as an opinion of them, but 'of' is only the join between the two halves.
annotation.definitionFit: A lens corrects or magnifies what you see.

entries.clue: Very little money for lace (10)

blocks.note: British idiom for a tiny budget, as in running a business on one

annotation.surface: Paying almost nothing for a piece of lace.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the same bootlace: a cheap thing, hence a tiny budget.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: running something on a bootlace's worth of money means on a very small budget.

entries.clue: Liver rodents left with first pair to finish pasta (10)

indicatorNotes.with first pair to finish: The first two letters are moved to the end.

annotation.surface: A grim dish of liver and rodents, with pasta to finish.
annotation.walkthrough: LIVER MICE L is built first, then its opening LI moves to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: these thin Italian strands, named for little worms, are one pasta.

entries.clue: Champagne maker limiting temperature and composition (5)

indicatorNotes.limiting: What limits something sets bounds on either side of it.

annotation.surface: A champagne house keeping its cellars at a controlled temperature.
annotation.walkthrough: Moët & Chandon is the champagne house, and the composition is musical.
annotation.definitionFit: A motet is a choral composition, usually sacred.

entries.clue: Watch part established to hold male South Africans? (10)

indicatorNotes.to hold: What holds something has it inside.

blocks.note: men from the Cape, a punning way to say South African men

annotation.surface: A timepiece built to fit South African men.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags CAPE MEN as an invented phrase: men of the Cape, at Africa's southern tip.
annotation.definitionFit: The escapement is the mechanism in a watch that releases the drive one tick at a time.

entries.clue: Fluid defence keeps closed round ball — nothing to row about (9)

indicatorNotes.keeps: What keeps something holds it inside.
indicatorNotes.round: One word round another encloses it.

blocks.note: a moat is a defensive ditch full of water
a door that is to is closed

annotation.surface: A water-filled moat enclosing a ball, and nothing to argue about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' is not a quarrel but rowing a boat: this craft needs no oars. 'Closed' is the old sense of a door being to.
annotation.definitionFit: A motorboat has an engine, so it is not something to be rowed about in.

entries.clue: Wool provided by farmer in Otago (6)

indicatorNotes.provided by: The letters are provided by the words that follow, running across them.

annotation.surface: Wool supplied by a sheep farmer in New Zealand.
annotation.walkthrough: Otago is a sheep-farming region of New Zealand, which makes the hidden merino apt.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the fine fleece of the Spanish-bred sheep is one of the best-known wools.

entries.clue: Cross-border crime force drops its case for unfortunate dead plant-eater (8)

indicatorNotes.drops its case: A word's case is its outer letters, which go.
indicatorNotes.for: The new case stands for the old, wrapping round what is left.

blocks.note: sad means unfortunate, as in a sad state

blocks.clueFragment: Cross-border crime force drops its case
blocks.note: EUROPOL, the EU police agency, without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Europol dropping a case of unfortunate death.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dead' goes with the definition, not the wordplay: a sauropod is an extinct, so dead, herbivore.
annotation.definitionFit: Sauropods were huge long-necked plant-eating dinosaurs, long extinct.

entries.clue: Absolute terror allowed (8)

blocks.note: a little terror is a naughty child, an imp

annotation.surface: Total terror being permitted.
annotation.walkthrough: A terror is a naughty child, not fear.
annotation.definitionFit: Implicit trust is absolute, unquestioning trust.

entries.clue: Left unfinished, religious image in place of pillars (7)

indicatorNotes.unfinished: An unfinished word lacks its last letter.

blocks.note: port is the left side of a ship

annotation.surface: A half-finished holy picture abandoned in a colonnade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' looks as if it goes with 'Left', but it works on the icon.
annotation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch whose roof is held up by columns.

entries.clue: Dent with Ford Prefect for the fifth time, not causing much damage? (6,8)

annotation.definition: Dent with Ford Prefect for the fifth time

blocks.clueFragment: Dent with Ford Prefect for the fifth time
blocks.note: the fifth Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy novel, starring Arthur Dent and Ford Prefect

annotation.surface: A minor car prang, dented by a Ford Prefect for the fifth time.
annotation.walkthrough: Dent and Ford Prefect look like a dented old British car, a Ford Prefect, but they are Douglas Adams's heroes. 'Mostly harmless' is the Guide's whole entry on Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: Mostly Harmless is Adams's fifth Hitchhiker book, and the phrase means doing little damage.

entries.clue: A Knight wooing Lady shuns embraces (6)

indicatorNotes.embraces: The words embrace the answer, holding it inside.

annotation.surface: A knight courting a lady who avoids his embraces.
annotation.walkthrough: The Knight is Gladys Knight, the American soul singer, not a knight in armour.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the American soul singer is one person surnamed Knight.

entries.clue: Defensive position’s vice-like grip (10)

blocks.note: split 6-and-4: a firm grip, like a vice's

annotation.surface: A fortress that holds on like a vice.
annotation.walkthrough: The first definition takes 's as is; the second reads the answer as two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fortress is a defensive position, and split in two the word is a firm grip.

entries.clue: One evades partygoer flipping in photo by a Glastonbury sight (12)

indicatorNotes.in: One thing in another sits inside it.
indicatorNotes.by: By means beside, so A TOR is placed next to what comes before.

blocks.note: Glastonbury Tor is a hill in Somerset, England

annotation.surface: A reveller dodging a festival photographer at Glastonbury.
annotation.walkthrough: Glastonbury suggests the music festival, but its sight is the Tor, a conical hill. The definition is a phrase: one who evades.
annotation.definitionFit: A prevaricator speaks evasively to avoid the truth.

entries.clue: Vain thugs regularly struck Christian martyr (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: Letters taken regularly are taken at even intervals, every other one.

annotation.surface: Conceited thugs repeatedly beating a saint.
annotation.walkthrough: St Vitus was martyred under Diocletian; St Vitus' dance is named after him.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Sicilian saint of St Vitus' dance was killed for his faith.

entries.clue: Divine Greek article cracked by Young Conservatives (5)

indicatorNotes.cracked by: What is cracked by something has that thing breaking into it.

annotation.surface: A Greek article cracked by young Tories.
annotation.walkthrough: Young Conservatives is the youth wing of Britain's Conservative Party.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the goddess of fortune is one divine figure of Greek myth.

entries.clue: Drive Golf into river (4)

indicatorNotes.into: G goes into the river's name.

blocks.note: the Ure, a river in Yorkshire

annotation.surface: Hitting a golf ball into a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a golf shot, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a drive in the sense of an inner impulse.

entries.clue: BBC pioneer backing row with husband (5)

indicatorNotes.backing: Backing is going in reverse, so the letters are read backwards.

annotation.surface: An early BBC figure supporting a married couple's quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: The row is a line, not a quarrel. John Reith was the BBC's first director-general.
annotation.definitionFit: Lord Reith founded the BBC's public-service ethos as its first head.

entries.clue: Not the last painting where a polar bear is black (9)

annotation.definition2: where a polar bear is black

blocks.note: the coat of paint beneath the final one

blocks.clueFragment: where a polar bear is black
blocks.note: under its white fur a polar bear's skin is black

annotation.surface: A painting of a black polar bear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Painting' is the act of painting, not a picture.
annotation.definitionFit: An undercoat is a layer of paint put on before the top coat.

entries.clue: One eats a lot of fish, large one in some pie filling (7)

annotation.definition: One eats a lot of fish

indicatorNotes.in: The letters go in the other word.

blocks.note: L for large, and I, the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Someone eating lots of fish, including a big one in a pie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A lot of fish' suggests a fish pie, but the fish is the pelican's diet.
annotation.definitionFit: Pelicans scoop up fish in their throat pouches.

entries.clue: Aesthetic judgment about rude photo that’s applied with brushing (10)

indicatorNotes.about: One word about another goes round it.
indicatorNotes.rude: Something rude is rough and unrefined, so the letters are knocked out of order.

blocks.note: good taste is a matter of aesthetic judgment

annotation.surface: A critic's verdict on an indecent picture painted with a brush.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rude photo' is not a saucy picture: 'rude' shakes up PHOTO.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: it is squeezed onto the brush, so it is applied with brushing.

entries.clue: ER I’d spoiled with TV set showing Top Gear feature? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.spoiled: Spoiled letters are damaged and reshaped.

annotation.surface: A Queen-spoiled TV that only shows Top Gear.
annotation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC motoring programme famous for its car reviews.
annotation.definitionFit: Top Gear's presenters test drive cars.
